name: CyBOK – The Cyber Security Body of Knowledge
description: CyBOK is a comprehensive, structured body of knowledge covering the foundational concepts and skills of cyber security.

knowledge_areas.title: Risk Management & Governance
knowledge_areas.description: Covers frameworks, principles, and practices to identify, assess, and manage cyber security risks at an organisational and strategic level.

chapters.title: Introduction to Risk
chapters.description: Foundational concepts of cyber risk including definitions, risk appetite, tolerance, and the difference between threat, vulnerability, and impact.

chapters.title: Risk Assessment
chapters.description: Methodologies for identifying and assessing cyber security risks including qualitative, quantitative, and hybrid approaches. Covers ISO 27005, NIST RMF, FAIR.

chapters.title: Risk Treatment
chapters.description: Options for responding to identified risks: avoidance, transfer, mitigation, and acceptance. Includes security control selection and implementation.

chapters.title: Governance Frameworks
chapters.description: Organisational governance over information security, including board-level accountability, security strategy, and standards such as ISO 27001/2 and COBIT.

chapters.title: Business Continuity and Resilience
chapters.description: Planning for continuity of operations during a cyber incident, including BCP, DRP, and resilience engineering.

chapters.title: Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk
chapters.description: Managing risks introduced by vendors, suppliers, and third-party integrations, including due diligence, contracts, and monitoring.

knowledge_areas.title: Law & Regulation
knowledge_areas.description: Examines legal frameworks, regulatory requirements, and compliance obligations relevant to cyber security.

chapters.title: Cybercrime and Computer Misuse
chapters.description: Criminal law relating to unauthorised access, computer misuse, and cybercrime offences. Covers the Computer Misuse Act, CFAA, and international equivalents.

chapters.title: Data Protection and Privacy Law
chapters.description: Legal frameworks governing how personal data is collected, stored and processed. Focuses on GDPR, UK DPA 2018, and principles such as lawful basis and data subject rights.

chapters.title: Sector-Specific Regulation
chapters.description: Regulatory obligations specific to sectors such as finance (FCA, PCI-DSS), healthcare (HIPAA), and critical infrastructure (NIS/NIS2 Directive).

chapters.title: Intellectual Property and Cyber
chapters.description: IP law as it applies to software, security research, vulnerability disclosure, and reverse engineering.

chapters.title: Jurisdiction and International Law
chapters.description: Cross-border application of cyber law, mutual legal assistance treaties, and the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime.

chapters.title: Liability and Contracts
chapters.description: Contractual and tortious liability for cyber security failures, including SLAs, indemnities, and professional regulatory exposure.

knowledge_areas.title: Human Factors
knowledge_areas.description: Covers the role of human behaviour, psychology, and organisational culture in cyber security.

chapters.title: Usable Security
chapters.description: Designing security systems that are both effective and usable, including security UX principles, warnings, and password systems.

chapters.title: Security Awareness and Training
chapters.description: Methods for building a security-aware workforce, including awareness campaigns, training effectiveness measurement, and phishing simulations.

chapters.title: Social Engineering
chapters.description: Psychological manipulation techniques used by attackers including phishing, vishing, pretexting, and physical intrusion.

chapters.title: Insider Threats
chapters.description: Risks from employees, contractors, and trusted insiders. Covers detection strategies, behavioural analytics, and mitigation approaches.

chapters.title: Organisational Culture
chapters.description: How security culture, leadership, norms, and incentive structures influence security outcomes in organisations.

chapters.title: Cognitive Biases and Decision-Making
chapters.description: How cognitive biases and heuristics affect security decisions by both end users and security professionals.

knowledge_areas.title: Privacy & Online Rights
knowledge_areas.description: Addresses principles, technologies, and legal dimensions of individual privacy and civil liberties in the digital world.

chapters.title: Privacy Concepts and Theory
chapters.description: Theoretical foundations of privacy, including definitions, taxonomies of privacy violations, and philosophical underpinnings.

chapters.title: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies
chapters.description: Technical tools for achieving privacy goals, including Tor, mix nets, differential privacy, and privacy-preserving computation.

chapters.title: Online Tracking and Profiling
chapters.description: Methods by which individuals are tracked online, including cookies, fingerprinting, and data brokers, and corresponding defences.

chapters.title: Surveillance and Government Interception
chapters.description: State surveillance capabilities, interception laws, lawful access requirements, and the tension between privacy and national security.

chapters.title: Anonymity and Censorship Resistance
chapters.description: Technologies enabling anonymous communication and access to censored content, including Tor, I2P, and circumvention tools.

chapters.title: Automated Decision Making and Biometrics
chapters.description: Privacy implications of AI-driven decisions and biometric data collection, including facial recognition and algorithmic scoring.

knowledge_areas.title: Malware & Attack Technologies
knowledge_areas.description: Covers techniques, tools, and technologies used by attackers to compromise systems.

chapters.title: Malware Classification and Lifecycle
chapters.description: Categories of malware including viruses, worms, Trojans, ransomware, spyware, and adware. Covers the infection and propagation lifecycle.

chapters.title: Exploitation Techniques
chapters.description: Vulnerability exploitation methods including buffer overflows, heap exploitation, use-after-free, format string bugs, and return-oriented programming (ROP).

chapters.title: Persistence and Evasion
chapters.description: Techniques attackers use to maintain access and evade detection, including rootkits, bootkits, registry persistence, fileless malware, and anti-analysis.

chapters.title: Command and Control Infrastructure
chapters.description: How attackers manage compromised systems remotely. Covers C2 protocols, domain generation algorithms, and peer-to-peer botnet architectures.

chapters.title: Ransomware and Cyber Extortion
chapters.description: Technical and operational mechanics of ransomware attacks, including encryption methods, payment infrastructure, and double-extortion techniques.

chapters.title: Advanced Persistent Threats
chapters.description: Long-running, targeted attack campaigns typically associated with nation-state actors. Covers APT tactics, zero-day exploitation, and campaign examples.

knowledge_areas.title: Adversarial Behaviours
knowledge_areas.description: Focuses on understanding attacker motivations, tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).

chapters.title: Threat Actor Taxonomy
chapters.description: Classification of adversaries by motivation (financial, espionage, hacktivism, sabotage) and capability, including nation-state, cybercriminal, and insider threat actors.

chapters.title: Attack Frameworks and Kill Chain
chapters.description: Models for understanding the stages of a cyber attack, including the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK framework.

chapters.title: Lateral Movement and Post-Exploitation
chapters.description: Techniques attackers use to move through a network after initial compromise, including privilege escalation, pass-the-hash, and Kerberoasting.

chapters.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence
chapters.description: Collecting, analysing, and actioning intelligence about threats and adversaries. Covers IoCs, TTPs, and structured sharing formats like STIX/TAXII.

chapters.title: Supply Chain Attacks
chapters.description: Targeting the software or hardware supply chain as an attack vector, including build system compromise, malicious packages, and firmware implants.

chapters.title: Disinformation and Influence Operations
chapters.description: Cognitive and information operations conducted by adversaries, including fake news, influence campaigns, and hybrid warfare.

knowledge_areas.title: Security Operations & Incident Management
knowledge_areas.description: Covers the detection, response, and recovery processes for cyber security incidents.

chapters.title: Security Monitoring Architecture
chapters.description: Design of security monitoring infrastructure including log aggregation, SIEM platforms, event correlation, and alerting pipelines.

chapters.title: Intrusion Detection and Prevention
chapters.description: Network and host-based IDS and IPS, detection methodologies (signature, anomaly, behavioural), and tuning to reduce false positives.

chapters.title: Threat Hunting
chapters.description: Proactive search for threats in the environment before alerts are triggered, using hypotheses, behavioural patterns, and analytics.

chapters.title: Incident Response Lifecycle
chapters.description: Structured approach to handling incidents, covering preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned (PICERL).

chapters.title: SOC Operations and Metrics
chapters.description: Organisation and management of a Security Operations Centre including shift structures, tier models, KPIs, and automation through SOAR.

chapters.title: Crisis Management and Communication
chapters.description: Communicating during a cyber incident internally and externally, including stakeholder management, regulatory notification, and public communications.

knowledge_areas.title: Forensics
knowledge_areas.description: Covers principles, methods, and tools used to collect, preserve, analyse, and present digital evidence.

chapters.title: Forensic Principles and Legal Admissibility
chapters.description: Foundational principles of digital forensics including chain of custody, seizure procedures, evidence integrity, and court admissibility standards.

chapters.title: Disk and File System Forensics
chapters.description: Acquisition and analysis of storage media, file system structures (NTFS, FAT, ext), deleted file recovery, and metadata analysis.

chapters.title: Memory Forensics
chapters.description: Capturing and analysing volatile memory (RAM) to recover processes, network connections, encryption keys, and malware artefacts.

chapters.title: Network Forensics
chapters.description: Reconstructing network activity from packet captures, flow records, and log files to support incident investigation.

chapters.title: Mobile Device Forensics
chapters.description: Extracting and analysing data from mobile devices including logical, file system, and physical acquisition techniques.

chapters.title: Cloud and Endpoint Forensics
chapters.description: Forensic challenges specific to cloud environments, ephemeral infrastructure, and enterprise endpoint tooling.

chapters.title: Anti-Forensics
chapters.description: Techniques used to hinder forensic analysis, including data wiping, timestomping, steganography, and encryption, and how to address them.

knowledge_areas.title: Cryptography
knowledge_areas.description: Covers the theoretical foundations of cryptographic systems used to protect information.

chapters.title: Foundations and Security Goals
chapters.description: Core cryptographic goals: confidentiality, integrity, authentication, and non-repudiation. Security definitions and proof techniques.

chapters.title: Symmetric Cryptography
chapters.description: Block ciphers (AES, DES), modes of operation (CBC, GCM, CTR), stream ciphers, and message authentication codes (HMAC).

chapters.title: Asymmetric Cryptography
chapters.description: Public-key cryptography foundations including RSA, Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), and Diffie-Hellman key exchange.

chapters.title: Hash Functions and MACs
chapters.description: Cryptographic hash functions (SHA-2, SHA-3), collision resistance, digital signatures (DSA, ECDSA), and HMAC.

chapters.title: Key Management and PKI
chapters.description: Generation, distribution, storage, and revocation of cryptographic keys. Public Key Infrastructure, certificate authorities, and OCSP/CRL.

chapters.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
chapters.description: Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist quantum computing attacks, including lattice-based, hash-based, and code-based schemes. NIST PQC standardisation.

knowledge_areas.title: Operating Systems & Virtualisation Security
knowledge_areas.description: Examines security features and vulnerabilities within operating systems and virtualisation platforms.

chapters.title: Operating System Security Architecture
chapters.description: Security primitives built into modern operating systems: protection rings, system calls, memory protection, and security boundaries.

chapters.title: Access Control Mechanisms
chapters.description: Discretionary, mandatory, and role-based access control implemented in operating systems including POSIX permissions, SELinux, and AppArmor.

chapters.title: OS Exploitation and Kernel Vulnerabilities
chapters.description: Common kernel vulnerabilities, privilege escalation techniques, exploit mitigations (ASLR, NX, SMEP), and kernel patching.

chapters.title: Virtualisation Security
chapters.description: Security of hypervisors (Type 1/2), VM isolation, hypervisor escape attacks, and secure deployment practices for virtualised environments.

chapters.title: Container Security
chapters.description: Security of containerised applications using Docker, Kubernetes, and related technologies. Namespace isolation, cgroups, and container escape vulnerabilities.

chapters.title: Trusted Execution Environments
chapters.description: Hardware-enforced secure enclaves including Intel SGX and ARM TrustZone, their security models, and attack surfaces.

knowledge_areas.title: Distributed Systems Security
knowledge_areas.description: Covers security challenges in systems composed of multiple interconnected components, including cloud and microservices.

chapters.title: Distributed System Fundamentals and Threats
chapters.description: Security challenges inherent to distributed architectures including partial failures, untrusted nodes, and Byzantine fault tolerance.

chapters.title: Cloud Security
chapters.description: Security models and threats for cloud deployments across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Shared responsibility, misconfiguration risks, and cloud-native controls.

chapters.title: Zero Trust Architecture
chapters.description: Principles and implementation of zero trust security for distributed systems, including identity-centric access, microsegmentation, and continuous verification.

chapters.title: Distributed Denial of Service
chapters.description: DDoS attack types, amplification, reflection, botnet-driven volumetric attacks, and mitigations at network and application layers.

chapters.title: Blockchain and Decentralised Systems
chapters.description: Security of blockchain-based systems including consensus attacks (51%, selfish mining), smart contract vulnerabilities, and wallet security.

chapters.title: Microservices and API Security
chapters.description: Security in service-oriented and microservices architectures, including API authentication (OAuth, JWT), rate limiting, and service mesh security.

knowledge_areas.title: Formal Methods for Security
knowledge_areas.description: Applies mathematical and logical techniques to specify, model, and verify security properties of systems and protocols.

chapters.title: Formal Specification of Security Properties
chapters.description: Expressing security requirements formally using languages such as Z, Alloy, and temporal logic.

chapters.title: Security Protocol Modelling and Analysis
chapters.description: Formal modelling and automated verification of cryptographic protocols using tools like ProVerif, Tamarin, and CPSA.

chapters.title: Model Checking for Security
chapters.description: Applying model checking (SPIN, NuSMV) to verify security properties in concurrent and distributed systems.

chapters.title: Type Systems and Information Flow
chapters.description: Using type-theoretic techniques to enforce security policies, prevent information leakage, and verify secure information flow statically.

chapters.title: Theorem Proving in Security
chapters.description: Application of interactive theorem provers (Coq, Isabelle/HOL) to prove correctness and security properties of algorithms and programs.

knowledge_areas.title: Authentication, Authorisation & Accountability
knowledge_areas.description: Covers techniques for establishing identity, enforcing permissions, and providing audit trails in information systems.

chapters.title: Authentication Fundamentals
chapters.description: The three authentication factors (knowledge, possession, inherence), authentication protocols, and the trade-offs between security and usability.

chapters.title: Password Security
chapters.description: Password storage (hashing, salting, bcrypt, PBKDF2), policies, credential stuffing and spraying attacks, and password managers.

chapters.title: Multi-Factor and Passwordless Authentication
chapters.description: MFA methods including TOTP, hardware tokens (FIDO2/WebAuthn), passkeys, biometrics, and their resistance to phishing.

chapters.title: Access Control Models
chapters.description: Discretionary (DAC), mandatory (MAC), role-based (RBAC), and attribute-based (ABAC) access control. Policy specification and enforcement.

chapters.title: Federated Identity and SSO
chapters.description: Federation protocols including SAML, OAuth 2.0, and OpenID Connect. Single sign-on architectures, trust models, and vulnerabilities.

chapters.title: Accountability and Audit Logging
chapters.description: Maintaining tamper-resistant audit trails to ensure accountability, including log management, integrity, and non-repudiation mechanisms.

knowledge_areas.title: Software Security
knowledge_areas.description: Covers principles, techniques, and best practices for developing secure software.

chapters.title: Memory Safety Vulnerabilities
chapters.description: Buffer overflows, stack and heap corruption, use-after-free, integer overflows, and format string vulnerabilities. Root causes and mitigations.

chapters.title: Injection Vulnerabilities
chapters.description: SQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection, and path traversal. Defences including parameterised queries, input validation, and output encoding.

chapters.title: Secure Coding Principles
chapters.description: Guidelines for writing secure code including least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults, and secure-by-design principles.

chapters.title: Static Application Security Testing (SAST)
chapters.description: Code analysis techniques for finding security vulnerabilities programmatically, including data flow analysis, taint tracking, and control flow analysis.

chapters.title: Dynamic Analysis and Fuzzing
chapters.description: Runtime testing approaches including coverage-guided fuzzing (AFL, libFuzzer), symbolic execution, and dynamic taint analysis.

chapters.title: Software Supply Chain Security
chapters.description: Risks from third-party dependencies, malicious packages, and build system compromise. SBOM, dependency auditing, and provenance tracking.

knowledge_areas.title: Web & Mobile Security
knowledge_areas.description: Examines security vulnerabilities and mitigations specific to web applications and mobile platforms.

chapters.title: Web Application Threat Model
chapters.description: Understanding the attack surface of web applications, the browser security model, same-origin policy, CORS, and common web threat categories.

chapters.title: Injection and Server-Side Attacks
chapters.description: SQL injection, NoSQL injection, command injection, Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), and XXE vulnerabilities with defences.

chapters.title: Client-Side Attacks
chapters.description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), clickjacking, DOM clobbering, and browser exploit techniques.

chapters.title: Authentication and Session Management
chapters.description: Web authentication vulnerabilities including session fixation, session hijacking, insecure JWT implementation, and broken authentication patterns.

chapters.title: Mobile Platform Security
chapters.description: Security architectures of Android and iOS including sandboxing, permissions, app signing, and secure storage. Common mobile vulnerabilities.

chapters.title: Mobile App Reverse Engineering
chapters.description: Reverse engineering Android APKs and iOS IPAs, bypassing certificate pinning, and analysing mobile app traffic.

knowledge_areas.title: Secure Software Lifecycle
knowledge_areas.description: Covers integration of security practices throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC).

chapters.title: Security Requirements Engineering
chapters.description: Eliciting and documenting security and privacy requirements from stakeholders, including misuse cases, abuse stories, and security user stories.

chapters.title: Threat Modelling
chapters.description: Structured approaches to identifying threats and selecting mitigations: STRIDE, PASTA, attack trees, and data flow diagrams.

chapters.title: Secure Design Principles
chapters.description: Applying security principles in architecture: least privilege, separation of privilege, economy of mechanism, and secure defaults.

chapters.title: DevSecOps and CI/CD Security
chapters.description: Integrating security into automated build and deployment pipelines, including SAST/DAST automation, secrets management, and infrastructure as code security.

chapters.title: Security Testing and Penetration Testing
chapters.description: Methodologies for security-focused testing including OWASP WSTG, penetration testing scopes, and reporting standards.

chapters.title: Vulnerability Disclosure and Patch Management
chapters.description: Responsible vulnerability disclosure programmes (CVD/bug bounty), patch release processes, and managing the window of exposure.

knowledge_areas.title: Applied Cryptography
knowledge_areas.description: Covers practical deployment and use of cryptographic protocols and systems in real-world applications.

chapters.title: TLS/SSL Protocol
chapters.description: TLS handshake, cipher suite negotiation, certificate validation, and vulnerabilities in prior versions (BEAST, POODLE, DROWN). TLS 1.3 improvements.

chapters.title: PKI Deployment and Certificate Management
chapters.description: Deploying and operating a certificate authority, certificate transparency logs, OCSP stapling, and CAA DNS records.

chapters.title: Secure Messaging Protocols
chapters.description: End-to-end encrypted messaging using the Signal Protocol, Double Ratchet, and forward secrecy. Comparison of messaging security properties.

chapters.title: Key Management in Practice
chapters.description: Operational aspects of key lifecycle management including generation, storage (HSM, KMS), rotation, backup, and revocation at scale.

chapters.title: Cryptographic API Design and Misuse
chapters.description: Common misuse of cryptographic APIs (ECB mode, nonce reuse, hardcoded keys). Principles for designing easy-to-use-securely cryptographic interfaces.

chapters.title: Advanced Protocols
chapters.description: Zero-knowledge proofs, secure multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption, and their emerging real-world applications.

knowledge_areas.title: Network Security
knowledge_areas.description: Covers security of computer networking, protocols, and infrastructure.

chapters.title: Network Protocol Security
chapters.description: Security weaknesses in foundational protocols (IP, TCP, UDP, ICMP) and routing protocols (BGP, OSPF). Spoofing, hijacking, and protocol manipulation attacks.

chapters.title: DNS Security
chapters.description: DNS cache poisoning, DNS hijacking, DNS over HTTPS/TLS, and DNSSEC deployment and operation.

chapters.title: Firewalls and Network Segmentation
chapters.description: Stateful firewalls, application-layer gateways, next-gen firewalls (NGFW), DMZ architectures, and microsegmentation strategies.

chapters.title: Wireless Network Security
chapters.description: Security of Wi-Fi standards (WPA2, WPA3, 802.1X), evil twin attacks, rogue access points, and enterprise wireless security.

chapters.title: VPNs and Secure Tunnelling
chapters.description: Site-to-site and remote access VPN technologies (IPsec, WireGuard, OpenVPN), split tunnelling, and authentication.

chapters.title: Network Traffic Analysis
chapters.description: Passive and active network monitoring for security, including flow analysis, deep packet inspection, and anomaly detection.

chapters.title: Software Defined Networking Security
chapters.description: Security implications of SDN architectures, control plane security, OpenFlow vulnerabilities, and network virtualisation security.

knowledge_areas.title: Hardware Security
knowledge_areas.description: Covers security properties and vulnerabilities of physical computing hardware.

chapters.title: Hardware Root of Trust
chapters.description: Establishing trust in hardware using TPMs, secure boot processes, measured boot, and hardware attestation mechanisms.

chapters.title: Side-Channel Attacks
chapters.description: Exploiting information leaked through power consumption, timing, electromagnetic emissions, and cache behaviour to extract secrets.

chapters.title: Fault Injection Attacks
chapters.description: Physically inducing faults via voltage glitching, clock glitching, and laser fault injection to bypass security checks.

chapters.title: Hardware Trojans and Supply Chain
chapters.description: Malicious hardware modifications inserted during manufacturing or distribution, detection methods, and supply chain trust.

chapters.title: Secure Enclaves and TEEs
chapters.description: Trusted Execution Environment technologies including Intel SGX, AMD SEV, and ARM TrustZone. Attacks including speculative execution (Spectre/Meltdown).

chapters.title: Embedded Systems and IoT Hardware
chapters.description: Hardware security of resource-constrained embedded devices, JTAG debugging interfaces, flash memory extraction, and physical hardening.

knowledge_areas.title: Cyber Physical Systems Security
knowledge_areas.description: Covers security of systems where cyber components directly interact with and control physical processes.

chapters.title: CPS Architecture and Threat Landscape
chapters.description: Architecture of cyber-physical systems, key differences from IT security, and the threat landscape including targeted attacks on CNI.

chapters.title: Industrial Control Systems and SCADA Security
chapters.description: Security of SCADA, DCS, and PLC systems. Common vulnerabilities, network segmentation, Purdue model, and ICS-specific attacks (Stuxnet, Triton).

chapters.title: IoT Security
chapters.description: Security challenges in IoT ecosystems including insecure-by-default devices, firmware vulnerabilities, constrained network protocols, and mass deployment risks.

chapters.title: Safety-Critical System Security
chapters.description: Intersection of functional safety and security in systems such as medical devices, automotive, and avionics (IEC 62443, DO-326A).

chapters.title: Resilience and Incident Response for CPS
chapters.description: Designing resilient CPS that degrade gracefully under attack. Incident response challenges and recovery for OT environments.

knowledge_areas.title: Physical Layer & Telecommunications Security
knowledge_areas.description: Examines the security of radio and physical communication channels, including wireless protocols and telecom infrastructure.

chapters.title: Physical Layer Fundamentals and Threats
chapters.description: Security of the physical transmission medium including interception, jamming, and exploitation of RF signals.

chapters.title: Cellular Network Security
chapters.description: Security architecture and vulnerabilities of 2G, 3G, 4G LTE, and 5G networks. IMSI catchers (Stingrays), SS7 vulnerabilities, and 5G security improvements.

chapters.title: TEMPEST and Emanation Security
chapters.description: Unintentional electromagnetic emissions from devices (TEMPEST/van Eck phreaking), shielding countermeasures, and EMSEC standards.

chapters.title: Satellite and Long-Range Communication Security
chapters.description: Security of satellite communications, GPS spoofing, and jamming. Security in VSAT, LoRa, and other long-range wireless protocols.

chapters.title: Telecommunications Regulatory and Legal Framework
chapters.description: Legal requirements and regulatory bodies governing telecommunications security, lawful interception, and emergency access.
